documents.title: UMass Dartmouth Guidelines on the Use of Generative AI
documents.stance_why: Both coders: restrict. The document says "Absent explicit permission or syllabus policy of an instructor, students are prohibited from using GAI" (ban unless permitted) and requires disclosure; it sets no tiers and only encourages faculty syllabus statements, so restrict and not delegates.
documents.summary: A short university-wide guideline on generative AI. Students may not use it without instructor or syllabus permission, must disclose and attribute any use, and may not present AI work as their own. It also defines GAI, warns of bias and false ease, and encourages faculty to state syllabus policies.

units.why: The opening says the policy will "center the human" in education and research; a statement of purpose and principles for the whole document, so P56 (framework/preamble).
units.anchor: firmly center the human as both agent and object of university education
units.resolution_why: A coded actor all, B admin. The sentence states what 'this policy aims to' do for the whole university, so it addresses everyone; actor all, phase general, P56 unchanged.

units.anchor: reaffirm existing university policies around academic integrity

units.why: Claims the tools "mimic, rather than replace or even imitate" human work and "do not have analytical or critical capacities"; a rationale about what AI is, nearest P96 (AI is not a person or author) though it is not about authorship rules, hence fit_note.

units.why: States tools "often reinforce bias and spread inaccurate or incorrect information", naming bias and inaccuracy; P53 for bias, while P31 (verify output) is not chosen because no instruction to verify is given.

units.why: Warns tools "can also provide a false sense of security or ease as users handover their own critical and creative faculties"; reliance on AI gives false confidence and cedes thinking, P43.

units.fit_note: Says false sense of security or ease and handing over critical faculties, not mastery exposed on exams. / Concerns false security and surrendering critical faculties generally, not mastery exposed on exams.

units.why: The aims list says the guidelines "Suggest ways faculty might clarify acceptable and prohibited AI use in syllabi and to their students", so they help instructors explain rules to students; P66 (explain rules to students), not P04 because no delegation sentence is stated here.
